implementation_notes: The JDK names the concept: a stream pipeline consists of a source, zero or more lazy intermediate operations and a terminal operation (Stream javadoc), so the stage list and its driver are replaced by `rows.stream().filter(..).map(..).map(..).collect(..)`. Intermediate operations are fused and lazy, the terminal operation drives the traversal, and parallel() switches the same pipeline to the common ForkJoinPool. Use the Function.andThen chain instead when the pipeline is a reusable value over a single object rather than a collection query.
pitfalls: A stream is consumed once: storing the stream instead of a Supplier and reusing it throws IllegalStateException, so pipelines that must run repeatedly should be stored as suppliers.
parallel() moves the pipeline onto the common ForkJoinPool, where stateful or interfering stage functions produce wrong results and unpredictable ordering.
Checked exceptions do not fit the functional interfaces, so any stage that can fail must wrap its exception, losing the checked-exception contract.

variants.name: Function composition with andThen (Java 8)
variants.implementation_notes: Function.andThen returns a composed function that applies this function first and the after function to the result, and compose() does the same in the opposite order; identity() is the empty pipeline (Function javadoc). Named method references or lambdas are the stages and the composed Function is the assembled pipeline value, which can be injected, cached or applied per request without re-creating a stream. Prefer it over a Stream when the payload is one object, when stages should be stored in a bean, or when no collection source exists.
pitfalls: A Function chain is homogeneous in practice: composing different in/out types forces wildcard or raw types, so heterogeneous stages lose compile-time checking.
andThen and compose compose in opposite directions; mixing them in one codebase silently reverses a chain.
Any stage throwing aborts the whole composed function - there is no per-stage recovery unless stages return a Result-like type.
